en.title: Delete in a Given Order While Keeping a Subsequence
en.description:
Delete characters of source one by one following order, a permutation of 1-based original indices; original indices are not renumbered after deletions. target is initially guaranteed to be a subsequence of source. Find the maximum number of leading deletions that can be performed consecutively while target remains a subsequence.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first two lines contain source and target (words without whitespace characters), and the last line contains a 1-based permutation of indices whose length equals the length of source. 1≤|source|≤100000, 1≤|target|≤|source|. Letter case is not arbitrarily restricted, and comparisons are case-sensitive.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 3; 1; 1. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Record the deletion time of each position and binary search on the number of deletions. When checking a candidate, ignore positions whose deletion time is ≤ the candidate, and greedily match the target subsequence.
